base.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        require(not base.stat().st_mode & 0o077,
                "private record directory must have mode 0700: " + str(base))
        name = ("run-" + time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime())
                + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])
        self.run_dir = base / name
        self.run_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
evidence.reason: At the pinned tip, `claim_run_dir` creates the record base and then the new run directory with `mkdir`, but never fsyncs the record base (or its parent when the base itself is newly created). `durable_write` flushes the recovery receipt and the run directory, so the directory entry in the record base for the new run directory can still be lost on power failure after admission while the host remains held, taking `prior_sha` and `original_triggers` with it. This is an implementation defect in the existing durable recovery behavior, not merely a new hardening request. The smallest compatible fix is to fsync the record base after creating the run directory, fsync the base parent when the base was newly created, and fail closed if either sync fails.
